verdict.outcome_rationale: This is a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct (TN): the held-out adaptability judge scored reward 0.0 because the agent's write-action log could not match the eleven-action oracle sequence [1][3]. The user request required booking Film Production Day on the upcoming Saturday, canceling conflicting appointments, emailing the Stockholm film-producer friend, reporting completion, and then—if the friend cannot make Saturday—accepting his proposed alternative, canceling conflicts on that day, and rescheduling the event [2][4]. The agent did execute the opening phase correctly: it deleted the Saturday Brand Partnership Meeting, created Film Production Day on 2024-10-19 with Åke Lindström as attendee, and sent him an email at ake.lindstrom@filmproduktion.se [5]. After that it spent many turns calling are_wait_for_notification, but every wait returned empty notifications and the simulation eventually exited with loop_dead without any reply from Åke ever appearing in the trajectory [6]. The reference solution's adaptability branch deletes the Saturday Film Production Day, clears five Thursday appointments, and recreates Film Production Day on 2024-10-17 08:00–20:00 once the environment event fires [2]; the agent performed none of those seven follow-on writes, its final calendar check still showed only the Saturday event, and it nonetheless sent the user a Done message claiming the work was finished [7][8]. With only four successful writes versus eleven oracle writes, the action-mode tool-count gate alone forces reward 0 even before semantic mismatches in the email subject and completion wording, so the agent did not genuinely solve this hard adaptability scenario.

The reference oracle for this adaptability scenario requires deleting the Saturday Film Production Day, canceling five Thursday appointments, and rescheduling Film Production Day to 2024-10-17 08:00–20:00 after an environment-triggered friend reply.
The task is graded in adaptability action mode, where mismatched per-tool write counts zero the reward before action matching proceeds.

def _check_tool_call_counts(
    oracle_actions: list[NormalizedAction],
    agent_actions: list[NormalizedAction],
) -> tuple[bool, dict[str, Any]]:
    aui_tool = "AgentUserInterface__send_message_to_user"
    oracle_counter = Counter(action.canonical_tool for action in oracle_actions)
    agent_counter = Counter(action.canonical_tool for action in agent_actions)

    oracle_aui_count = oracle_counter.pop(aui_tool, 0)
    agent_aui_count = agent_counter.pop(aui_tool, 0)
    counts_match = (
        oracle_counter == agent_counter
        and oracle_aui_count
        <= agent_aui_count
        <= oracle_aui_count + EXTRA_SEND_MESSAGE_TO_USER_ALLOWED
    )
